from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Attention Scores (Dot-Product)", [
            "Dot-products measure word relevance.", 
            "Softmax converts scores into weights.", 
            "High relevance creates a spotlight."
        ])
        
        self.lecture.set_opacity(1)

        # Animation Setup
        vec_q = Vector([1, 0], color=YELLOW)
        vec_k = Vector([0.5, 0.8], color=BLUE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_q), FadeIn(vec_k))
        self.play(Rotate(vec_k, angle=-0.5), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Projection line
        proj_val = 0.7
        proj_line = DashedLine(vec_k.get_end(), [vec_k.get_end()[0], 0, 0], color=PURPLE)
        self.play(Create(proj_line))
        
        val_text = MathTex("Score = 0.7", color="#FF00FF").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(val_text, "D4")
        self.play(Write(val_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        softmax_text = Text("Softmax(Score) -> 0.85", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(softmax_text, "E4")
        self.play(FadeIn(softmax_text))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GOLD)
        
        spotlight = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GOLD, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(spotlight, "B4")
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(spotlight))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture", 
                          ["One spotlight isn't enough context.", 
                           "Multiple heads see different relations.", 
                           "They act like a detective team."])
        
        # Colors for semantic consistency (B006)
        COLOR_HEAD1 = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_HEAD2 = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_HEAD3 = "#FFFF00"
        
        # Initial reveal
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display three parallel attention heads
        head1 = Square(side_length=1.5, color=COLOR_HEAD1).set_fill(COLOR_HEAD1, opacity=0.3)
        head2 = Square(side_length=1.5, color=COLOR_HEAD2).set_fill(COLOR_HEAD2, opacity=0.3)
        head3 = Square(side_length=1.5, color=COLOR_HEAD3).set_fill(COLOR_HEAD3, opacity=0.3)
        heads = VGroup(head1, head2, head3).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(heads, "B4", "C6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(heads))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_HEAD1).set_opacity(1)
        # Represent Q, K, V mechanism in each head (using concrete-like markers)
        qkv = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, 1) for _ in range(9)])
        qkv.arrange_in_grid(3, 3)
        self.place_in_area(qkv, "E4", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(qkv))
        self.play(Indicate(heads))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_HEAD2).set_opacity(1)
        # Show head outputs concatenating into single vector
        output_vec = Rectangle(width=4.0, height=0.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, 0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(output_vec, "D5", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Transform(heads, output_vec))
        self.play(FadeOut(qkv))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Transformer Core", [
            "Attention creates context-aware word embeddings.", 
            "This enables deep language understanding.", 
            "The foundation of modern Transformers."
        ])
        
        # Mobjects
        encoder_block = Rectangle(width=4, height=4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.2)
        multi_head_block = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]), FadeIn(encoder_block))
        self.place_in_area(encoder_block, 'B2', 'E5')
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(multi_head_block, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(multi_head_block))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        # Animate data flow (simple particles)
        flow = VGroup(*[Dot(color=BLUE) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(flow, 'E3')
        self.play(flow.animate.shift(UP * 2), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#0000FF")

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students (computer science or general STEM background)

sections.title: The Intuition: Contextual Awareness
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'selective focus.' Explain that just as humans focus on specific words to understand a sentence, models must determine which parts of an input are relevant to others.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' the model must link 'it' to 'animal' rather than 'street'.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
sections.content: Define the Q, K, and V vectors. Explain them via an analogy: Q (Query) is what I am looking for; K (Key) is what information is available; V (Value) is the actual content once a match is found.
sections.example: Like a library database: You type a search query (Q), the system matches it against book titles (K), and returns the actual page content (V) based on the relevance score.

sections.title: Visualizing Attention Scores (Dot-Product)
sections.content: Explain how relevance is calculated using the dot product between Q and K. Introduce the Softmax function as a 'weighting machine' that converts raw scores into percentages that sum to 100%.
sections.example: Visualized as a heat map matrix: High-relevance words glow bright gold, while irrelevant ones fade to dark blue, creating a 'focus spotlight' on the sentence.

sections.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture
sections.content: Explain why one 'spotlight' isn't enough. Multi-head attention allows the model to look at different parts of the data simultaneously—one head might focus on grammar, another on sentiment, another on entities.
sections.example: Like a team of detectives: Detective A focuses on who did it, Detective B focuses on where it happened, and Detective C focuses on when it happened. Together, they build a complete report.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Transformer Core
sections.content: Summarize how these weighted values (V) are combined to form a new, context-aware representation for each word, allowing the model to 'understand' complex relationships.
sections.example: A final animation showing a jumbled 'bag of words' entering the attention layer and emerging as a structured, meaningful sequence ready for text generation.
